newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures plunge on stronger yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures plunge on stronger yen.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply lower on Tuesday, with all contracts down by the daily 500 yen limit as the yen's rise against the dollar triggered heavy selling from local investors, traders said.
The benchmark May 1998 contract closed down 500 yen at 13,480 yen per tonne. The day's estimated trade volume was 103,220 lots.

All contracts fell sharply, due to active selling orders from local investors from the opening, traders said. "The market factor today was the strong yen. That's it," a brokerage house trader said. Traders said the distant month is unlikely to fall sharply below the 13,000 yen level.
At 0925 GMT, the spot May corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was at $2.92-1/2 per bushel, down from the $2.93-1/4 Monday close.
The spot May soybean contract on the CBOT overnight trading system stood at $8.69 per bushel, against the previous close of $8.67-1/2.
